headline: Anthropic reports internal tests of persistent memory and offline correction for agents
summary: Anthropic’s 6 November engineering article describes persistent agent memory as a hierarchy of session logs, notes, linked representations and selectively injected context, with offline “dreaming” used to correct or reorganize it. The company reports gains on CL-Bench, a Pokémon navigation example, and internal document-corpus evaluations, including cases where wiki organization improved retrieval and cases where it added no clear benefit or grew larger than its sources. The results are first-party and task-specific; they do not establish general production reliability or transfer.
